chapters.title: Tell It Not in Gath
chapters.html:
Micah 1

The LORD Comes Out of His Place

1The word of the LORD that came to Micah of Moresheth in the days of Jotham, Ahaz and Hezekiah, kings of Judah, which he saw concerning Samaria and Jerusalem.

2Hear, you peoples, all of you;
listen, earth, and all that fills it;
let the Lord GOD be a witness against you,
the Lord from His holy temple.

3For the LORD is about to come out from His place;
He will come down and tread on the heights of the earth.

4The mountains will melt under Him,
and the valleys split open,
like wax before the fire,
like water poured down a slope.

5All this is for the transgression of Jacob
and for the sins of the house of Israel.
What is the transgression of Jacob?
Is it not Samaria?
What are the high places of Judah?
Are they not Jerusalem?

6So I will make Samaria a heap in the open field,
a place for planting vineyards;
I will pour her stones down into the valley
and lay bare her foundations.

7All her carved images will be smashed to pieces,
all her wages will be burned with fire,
and I will make all her idols a desolation;
for she gathered them from a prostitute's wages,
and to a prostitute's wages they will return.

I Will Lament and Howl

8For this I will lament and howl;
I will go stripped and naked;
I will make a lament like the jackals
and a mourning like the ostriches.

9For her wounds are incurable;
it has come to Judah;
it has reached the gate of my people,
to Jerusalem.

10Tell it not in Gath;
do not weep at all;
in Beth-leaphrah
roll yourself in the dust.

11Pass on, inhabitant of Shaphir,
in shameful nakedness;
the inhabitant of Zaanan has not come out;
the wailing of Beth-ezel
will take from you its standing place.

12For the inhabitant of Maroth
writhes, waiting for good,
because disaster has come down from the LORD
to the gate of Jerusalem.

13Harness the chariot to the steeds,
inhabitant of Lachish;
she was the beginning of sin
for the daughter of Zion,
for in you were found
the transgressions of Israel.

14Therefore you will give parting gifts
to Moresheth-gath;
the houses of Achzib will be a deceitful brook
to the kings of Israel.

15I will yet bring the conqueror upon you,
inhabitant of Mareshah;
the glory of Israel
will come as far as Adullam.

16Make yourself bald and shave your hair
for the children you delight in;
make your baldness as wide as the eagle's,
for they have gone from you into exile.

Notes

  • v1 "Micah of Moresheth… Jotham, Ahaz and Hezekiah" — Mikhah is short for Mikhayahu, who is like the LORD?, and Jeremiah's text writes it long, Mikhayah, where it is read Mikhah (Jeremiah 26:18). The Greek calls him Meichaias, the name it gives Micaiah son of Imlah (1 Kings 22:8). He is remembered by name in Jeremiah's trial, when some of the elders of the land said, Micah of Moresheth prophesied in the days of Hezekiah king of Judah (Jeremiah 26:17–18). The kings are those of Hosea 1:1 after Uzziah. Moresheth is the Moresheth-gath of v14.

  • vv10–12 "Tell it not in Gath… Beth-leaphrah… Shaphir… Zaanan… Beth-ezel… Maroth" — Tell it not in Gath is David's lament for Saul (2 Samuel 1:20). Then each town hears its name turned against it: Beit le-Afrah, house of dust, rolls in afar, dust (the read form, roll yourself; written, I have rolled); Shafir, beautiful, goes in shameful nakedness; Tsa'anan sounds like yatsa, come out, and does not come out; Marot, bitterness, waits for good. V11's last line is obscure: Beit ha-Etsel, house beside, takes its emdah, standing place, away. The Greek reads several names as words.

chapters.title: The One Who Breaks Through
chapters.html:
Micah 2

Woe to Those Who Devise Wickedness

1Woe to those who devise wickedness
and work evil on their beds!
In the morning light they do it,
for their hand has the power.

2They covet fields and seize them,
and houses, and take them away;
they oppress a man and his house,
a man and his inheritance.

3Therefore this is what the LORD says:
I am about to devise disaster against this family,
from which you cannot remove your necks;
you will not walk with your heads high,
for it is an evil time.

4On that day they will take up a taunt against you
and raise a lament:
"It is over; we are utterly ruined;
He changes the portion of my people.
How He takes it away from me!
To the faithless He divides our fields."

5Therefore you will have no one
to cast the measuring line by lot
in the assembly of the LORD.

Do Not Preach

6"Do not preach," they preach.
"One should not preach of such things;
disgrace will not overtake us."

7Should this be said, house of Jacob?
Is the Spirit of the LORD cut short?
Are these His deeds?
Do not My words do good
to the one who walks uprightly?

8But lately My people have risen up as an enemy:
you strip the cloak off the garment
from those who pass by trusting,
like men returning from war.

9The women of My people you drive out
from their pleasant houses;
from their young children you take away
My splendor forever.

10Get up and go,
for this is not the place of rest;
because of uncleanness it will destroy
with a grievous destruction.

11If a man walking after wind and lies should deceive:
"I will preach to you of wine and strong drink,"
he would be the preacher for this people!

I Will Gather Jacob

12I will surely gather all of you, Jacob;
I will surely assemble the remnant of Israel;
I will put them together like sheep in a fold,
like a flock in the middle of its pasture;
they will hum with people.

13The one who breaks through will go up before them;
they will break through and pass the gate
and go out by it;
their king will pass on before them,
the LORD at their head.

Notes

  • v6 "'Do not preach,' they preach" — al tattifu yattifun. Nataf is drip, and of speech preach, the verb Amaziah used to Amos, do not preach against the house of Isaac (Amos 7:16). Who says it, the people to the prophets or one prophet to another, the line does not mark. Lo yissag kelimmot is disgrace will not overtake us, or disgrace will not turn back; the Greek has do not weep with tears.

  • vv8–9 "My people have risen up as an enemy… from their young children you take away My splendor forever" — obscure. As the lines stand, the powerful treat their own people as an enemy, stripping cloaks from travelers who expect no harm, as if they were spoil of war, and driving women and children from their houses. Hadari, My splendor, is the LORD's: what He gave the children is taken from them for good.

  • v13 "The one who breaks through will go up before them… their king… the LORD at their head" — ha-porets, the one who breaks through, has the name of Perez, How you have breached — a breach upon you!… He called his name Perez (Genesis 38:29), from whom David came (Ruth 4:18), and the words of David's victory, The LORD has broken through my enemies before me (2 Samuel 5:20). Whether their king and the LORD are one leader or two, the verse does not say.

chapters.title: Zion Shall Be Plowed as a Field
chapters.html:
Micah 3

The Heads of Jacob

1I said:
Hear, please, you heads of Jacob
and rulers of the house of Israel!
Is it not for you to know justice?

2You who hate good and love evil,
who tear the skin off them
and the flesh off their bones,

3who eat the flesh of my people,
strip their skin off them,
break their bones,
and chop them up like meat for the pot,
like flesh in a cauldron —

4then they will cry out to the LORD,
but He will not answer them;
He will hide His face from them at that time,
because they have made their deeds evil.

The Prophets Who Lead My People Astray

5This is what the LORD says concerning the prophets
who lead My people astray,
who, when they have something to bite with their teeth,
cry "Peace!",
but consecrate war against whoever puts nothing into their mouths:

6Therefore it will be night for you, without vision,
and darkness for you, without divination;
the sun will go down on the prophets,
and the day will grow dark over them.

7The seers will be ashamed,
and the diviners disgraced;
they will all cover their upper lips,
for there is no answer from God.

8But as for me, I am filled with power,
with the Spirit of the LORD,
and with justice and might,
to declare to Jacob his transgression
and to Israel his sin.

Because of You

9Hear this, please, you heads of the house of Jacob
and rulers of the house of Israel,
who detest justice
and make crooked all that is straight,

10who build Zion with blood
and Jerusalem with injustice.

11Her heads judge for a bribe,
her priests teach for a price,
and her prophets divine for money;
yet they lean on the LORD and say,
"Is not the LORD among us?
No disaster will come upon us."

12Therefore, because of you,
Zion shall be plowed as a field;
Jerusalem shall become a heap of ruins,
and the mountain of the house a wooded height.

Notes

  • v5 "who, when they have something to bite with their teeth, cry 'Peace!'" — ha-noshkhim be-shinneihem, word for word who bite with their teeth; nashakh is the verb of the snake's bite (Amos 5:19; 9:3). A meal buys shalom, the word Jeremiah's prophets sold, saying, "Peace, peace," when there is no peace (Jeremiah 6:14). No meal, and they consecrate war, the holy war of Consecrate war against her! (Jeremiah 6:4).

  • v12 "Zion shall be plowed as a field… a wooded height" — this verse is quoted word for word in Jeremiah's trial: Micah of Moresheth prophesied in the days of Hezekiah… Zion shall be plowed as a field (Jeremiah 26:18). The elders go on: Did he not fear the LORD and plead with the LORD, so that the LORD relented of the disaster that He had pronounced against them? (Jeremiah 26:19). Bamot ya'ar, a wooded height, says bamot again, the heights of 1:3 and 1:5.

chapters.title: Swords into Plowshares
chapters.html:
Micah 4

The Mountain of the LORD's House

1And it shall come to pass in the last days
that the mountain of the LORD's house shall be established
as the highest of the mountains;
it shall be lifted up above the hills,
and peoples shall stream to it.

2Many nations shall go and say,
"Come, let us go up to the mountain of the LORD,
and to the house of the God of Jacob,
that He may teach us His ways,
and that we may walk in His paths."
For out of Zion shall go forth instruction,
and the word of the LORD from Jerusalem.

3He shall judge between many peoples,
and decide for strong nations far away;
they shall beat their swords into plowshares,
and their spears into pruning hooks;
nation shall not lift up sword against nation,
nor shall they learn war anymore.

4But they shall sit, each man under his vine
and under his fig tree,
and no one shall make them afraid;
for the mouth of the LORD of hosts has spoken.

5For all the peoples walk,
each in the name of its god,
but we will walk in the name of the LORD our God
forever and ever.

The Lame and the Outcast

6On that day, declares the LORD,
I will gather the lame
and assemble the outcast,
and those I have harmed;

7I will make the lame a remnant,
and the cast-off a strong nation;
and the LORD will reign over them on Mount Zion
from now on and forever.

8As for you, tower of the flock,
hill of the daughter of Zion,
to you it will come;
the former dominion will come,
the kingdom of the daughter of Jerusalem.

Writhe, Daughter of Zion

9Now why do you cry aloud?
Is there no king in you?
Has your counselor perished,
that pain has seized you like a woman in labor?

10Writhe and burst forth, daughter of Zion,
like a woman in labor;
for now you will go out of the city
and live in the open field;
you will go to Babylon;
there you will be rescued;
there the LORD will redeem you
from the power of your enemies.

11Now many nations are gathered against you,
who say, "Let her be polluted,
and let our eyes gaze on Zion."

12But they do not know the thoughts of the LORD,
and they do not understand His counsel,
for He has gathered them like sheaves to the threshing floor.

13Rise and thresh, daughter of Zion,
for I will make your horn iron
and your hoofs bronze;
you will crush many peoples,
and I will devote their gain to the LORD,
their wealth to the Lord of all the earth.

Notes

  • vv1–3 "the mountain of the LORD's house… swords into plowshares" — the same oracle stands in Isaiah 2:2–4, nearly word for word. The two differ in small things that show: here peoples shall stream to it, where Isaiah has all the nations; many nations shall go, where Isaiah has many peoples; and Micah alone has strong nations far away. Isaiah goes on, House of Jacob, come, let us walk in the light of the LORD (Isaiah 2:5); Micah goes on with v4. Be-acharit ha-yamim, in the last days, is the phrase Hosea gives as in the end of days (Hosea 3:5).

  • v8 "tower of the flock, hill of the daughter of Zion" — Migdal Eder, Tower of the Flock, is the place where Jacob camped after Rachel was buried on the road to Ephrath — that is Bethlehem: Israel pulled up and pitched his tent beyond Migdal-eder (Genesis 35:19, 21). Ophel, hill, is the name of a height of Jerusalem, the wall of Ophel (2 Chronicles 27:3). The former dominion is the kingdom as it once was; the Greek adds from Babylon.

chapters.title: But You, Bethlehem Ephrathah
chapters.html:
Micah 5

The Ruler from Bethlehem

1Now gather in your troops, daughter of troops;
a siege is laid against us;
with a rod they strike the judge of Israel
on the cheek.

2But you, Bethlehem Ephrathah,
too small to be among the clans of Judah,
from you shall come out for Me
one who is to be ruler in Israel,
whose goings out are from ancient times,
from the days of old.

3Therefore He will give them up
until the time when she who is in labor has given birth;
then the rest of his brothers will return
to the sons of Israel.

4He will stand and shepherd in the strength of the LORD,
in the majesty of the name of the LORD his God;
and they will live secure,
for now he will be great
to the ends of the earth.

5This one will be peace.
When Assyria comes into our land
and treads on our strongholds,
we will raise against him seven shepherds
and eight princes of men.

6They will shepherd the land of Assyria with the sword,
and the land of Nimrod at its gates;
and he will rescue us from Assyria
when it comes into our land
and treads within our border.

The Remnant of Jacob

7The remnant of Jacob will be
among many peoples
like dew from the LORD,
like downpours on the plants,
which do not wait for man
or delay for the sons of men.

8The remnant of Jacob will be among the nations,
among many peoples,
like a lion among the beasts of the forest,
like a young lion among the flocks of sheep,
which, when it goes through, tramples and tears,
and there is no one to rescue.

9Your hand will be lifted up over your adversaries,
and all your enemies will be cut off.

I Will Cut Off

10And it shall come to pass on that day,
declares the LORD,
that I will cut off your horses from among you
and destroy your chariots;

11I will cut off the cities of your land
and tear down all your fortresses;

12I will cut off sorceries from your hand,
and you will have no more soothsayers;

13I will cut off your carved images
and your standing stones from among you,
and you will no longer bow down
to the work of your hands;

14I will uproot your sacred poles from among you
and destroy your cities.

15In anger and wrath I will execute vengeance
on the nations that have not listened.

Notes

  • v1 "Now gather in your troops, daughter of troops… strike the judge of Israel on the cheek" — in the Hebrew text this verse is 4:14, and vv2–15 are 5:1–14; the English numbering is followed. Titgodedi bat gedud plays on one sound: gadad is to gather in troops, as Jeremiah's people trooped to the house of a prostitute (Jeremiah 5:7), and to gash oneself in grief, You shall not gash yourselves (Deuteronomy 14:1). The Greek has the daughter will be walled in with a wall. The judge struck on the cheek is how the prophet before Micah was treated: Zedekiah… struck Micaiah on the cheek (1 Kings 22:24). From the shofet, judge, struck down, the next verse turns to the moshel, ruler, to come.

  • v2 "But you, Bethlehem Ephrathah, too small to be among the clans of Judah" — Ephrathah is David's town, that Ephrathite of Bethlehem in Judah whose name was Jesse (1 Samuel 17:12), and the road where Rachel was buried, the road to Ephrath — that is Bethlehem (Genesis 35:19). Tsa'ir, small, is the word for the younger son in the oracle over Rebekah's twins, the elder shall serve the younger (Genesis 25:23). Matthew gives the verse in other words: You, Bethlehem, land of Judah, are by no means least among the rulers of Judah; for from you will come a ruler who will shepherd My people Israel (Matthew 2:6). Alfei, the clans, has the letters of allufei, chiefs; by no means least turns too small around; and who will shepherd My people Israel are the words said to David, You shall shepherd My people Israel (2 Samuel 5:2).

  • v2 "whose goings out are from ancient times, from the days of old" — motsa'otav, his goings out, the word of Israel's starting points in the wilderness (Numbers 33:2): where he comes from. Mi-yemei olam, from the days of old, are the words of Amos's promise to rebuild David's fallen booth as in the days of old (Amos 9:11). Olam runs from long ago to forever: Micah has it as forever and ever (4:5) and from now on and forever (4:7).

  • vv5–6 "This one will be peace… seven shepherds and eight princes of men… the land of Nimrod" — ve-hayah zeh shalom: zeh, this one, the ruler of vv2–4, or this of what follows; the Greek has this will be peace. Seven, then eight, is the counting of Amos's for three… and for four (Amos 1:3): enough, and one more. Nesikhei, princes, is the word of the princes of Sihon (Joshua 13:21). Assyria is called the land of Nimrod, from whose kingdom went out Asshur (Genesis 10:11). Shepherd… with the sword is the shepherd's word turned to war. Bi-ftacheha, at its gates; the Greek has in its trench.

chapters.title: What the LORD Requires
chapters.html:
Micah 6

The LORD's Case

1Hear, please, what the LORD says:
Rise, plead your case before the mountains,
and let the hills hear your voice.

2Hear, you mountains, the LORD's case,
you enduring foundations of the earth;
for the LORD has a case against His people,
and He will argue it out with Israel.

3My people, what have I done to you?
How have I wearied you?
Answer against Me!

4For I brought you up from the land of Egypt
and redeemed you from the house of slaves;
and I sent before you
Moses, Aaron and Miriam.

5My people, remember what Balak king of Moab devised,
and what Balaam son of Beor answered him,
from Shittim to Gilgal,
so that you may know the righteous acts of the LORD.

What Does the LORD Require?

6With what shall I come before the LORD
and bow myself before God on high?
Shall I come before Him with burnt offerings,
with calves a year old?

7Will the LORD be pleased with thousands of rams,
with ten thousands of rivers of oil?
Shall I give my firstborn for my transgression,
the fruit of my body for the sin of my soul?

8He has told you, O man, what is good;
and what does the LORD require of you
but to do justice, and to love loyal love,
and to walk humbly with your God?

Wicked Scales

9The voice of the LORD calls to the city,
and sound wisdom sees Your name:
Hear the rod, and the One who appointed it!

10Are there still, in the house of the wicked,
treasures of wickedness,
and the scant ephah that is cursed?

11Shall I count pure the one with wicked scales,
with a bag of false weights?

12Her rich men are full of violence;
her inhabitants speak lies,
and their tongue is deceit in their mouth.

13So I in turn have struck you with a sickening blow,
making you desolate because of your sins.

14You will eat and not be satisfied,
and your hunger will be inside you;
you will put away but not save,
and what you save I will give to the sword.

15You will sow but not reap;
you will tread olives but not anoint yourself with oil,
and tread grapes for new wine but not drink the wine.

16The statutes of Omri are kept,
and all the works of the house of Ahab,
and you have walked in their counsels;
so I will make you a desolation,
and her inhabitants a thing to be hissed at,
and you will bear the scorn of My people.

Notes

  • v8 "what does the LORD require of you but to do justice, and to love loyal love, and to walk humbly with your God?" — Moses asked it first: And now, Israel, what does the LORD your God ask of you but to fear the LORD your God, to walk in all His ways and to love Him (Deuteronomy 10:12). Ahavat chesed, to love loyal love, is the chesed the LORD desires over sacrifice, For I desire loyal love and not sacrifice (Hosea 6:6), and the chesed He delights in (7:18). Hatsnea lekhet, to walk humbly, from tsana, modest, careful, as in with the humble is wisdom (Proverbs 11:2); the Greek has to be ready to walk with the Lord your God. Adam, O man: a human being, any one.

  • v9 "sound wisdom sees Your name: Hear the rod, and the One who appointed it!" — obscure. Ve-tushiyyah yir'eh shemekha, and sound wisdom sees Your name; yir'eh, sees, has the letters of yir'ah, fear, and the Greek has He will save those who fear His name. Shim'u matteh u-mi ye'adah, hear the rod, and who appointed it: matteh is a rod and also a tribe, and the Greek has hear, O tribe. Ye'adah, appointed it, is feminine, which may point back to the city. As the lines stand, the rod is the punishment, and the city is told to heed it and the One who set it.

  • vv13–15 "a sickening blow… You will eat and not be satisfied… you will tread olives but not anoint yourself with oil" — the curses of the law come due: you will eat and not be satisfied (Leviticus 26:26), and you will not anoint yourself with oil, for your olives will drop off (Deuteronomy 28:40), as Amos also said of the vineyards (Amos 5:11). Ve-yeshchakha, your hunger, is found only here, and its sense is a guess from the line; the Greek has it will grow dark in you.

chapters.title: Who Is a God Like You?
chapters.html:
Micah 7

Woe to Me

1Woe to me! For I have become
like the gatherings of summer fruit,
like the gleanings of the grape harvest:
there is no cluster to eat,
no first-ripe fig that my soul desires.

2The faithful one has perished from the land,
and there is no one upright among men;
they all lie in wait for blood;
each hunts his brother with a net.

3Their hands are on evil, to do it well:
the prince asks, and the judge, for a payment,
and the great man speaks the desire of his soul;
so they weave it together.

4The best of them is like a briar,
the most upright worse than a hedge of thorns.
The day of your watchmen, your punishment, has come;
now will be their confusion.

5Do not trust a neighbor;
do not rely on a close friend;
from her who lies in your arms
guard the doors of your mouth.

6For son treats father with contempt,
daughter rises against her mother,
daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law;
a man's enemies are the men of his own house.

I Will Watch for the LORD

7But as for me, I will watch for the LORD;
I will wait for the God of my salvation;
my God will hear me.

8Do not rejoice over me, my enemy;
though I have fallen, I will rise;
though I sit in darkness,
the LORD is my light.

9I will bear the rage of the LORD,
because I have sinned against Him,
until He pleads my cause
and carries out justice for me.
He will bring me out to the light;
I will look on His righteousness.

10Then my enemy will see,
and shame will cover her,
she who said to me,
"Where is the LORD your God?"
My eyes will look on her;
now she will be trampled down
like the mud of the streets.

A Day for Building Your Walls

11A day for building your walls!
On that day the boundary will be far off.

12On that day they will come to you,
from Assyria and the cities of Egypt,
and from Egypt to the River,
from sea to sea and from mountain to mountain.

13But the earth will become a desolation
because of its inhabitants,
for the fruit of their deeds.

Who Is a God Like You?

14Shepherd Your people with Your rod,
the flock of Your inheritance,
who dwell alone, a forest
in the middle of Carmel;
let them graze in Bashan and Gilead
as in the days of old.

15As in the days when you came out of the land of Egypt,
I will show him wonders.

16The nations will see and be ashamed
of all their might;
they will lay their hand on their mouth;
their ears will be deaf.

17They will lick the dust like a snake,
like things that crawl on the earth;
they will come quaking out of their strongholds;
they will come trembling to the LORD our God,
and they will fear You.

18Who is a God like You,
carrying guilt and passing over transgression
for the remnant of His inheritance?
He does not hold on to His anger forever,
for He delights in loyal love.

19He will again have compassion on us;
He will tread our iniquities under foot.
You will cast all their sins
into the depths of the sea.

20You will give truth to Jacob,
loyal love to Abraham,
as You swore to our fathers
from ancient days.

Notes

  • vv3–4 "the judge, for a payment… so they weave it together… worse than a hedge of thorns" — partly obscure. Ba-shillum, for a payment, is the word of Hosea's the days of repayment have come (Hosea 9:7). Va-ye'abbetuha, they weave it together, is found only here; it is the root of avot, a cord, as in bands of love (Hosea 11:4): the prince, the judge and the great man twist their wants into one rope. Mesukhah, a hedge of thorns, is the word of the way of a sluggard is like a hedge of thorns (Proverbs 15:19), spelled there with sin for samekh; and chedeq, briar, is the thorn of that verse; for like a briar the Greek has like a moth devouring. Your watchmen are the prophets, as the LORD said to Ezekiel, I have made you a watchman for the house of Israel (Ezekiel 3:17): the day they warned of has come. Mevukhatam, their confusion, is Isaiah's a day of tumult and trampling and confusion (Isaiah 22:5).

  • vv11–13 "the boundary will be far off… from Assyria and the cities of Egypt… from sea to sea" — yirchak choq is obscure. Choq is a decree, and a boundary set, as in when He assigned to the sea its limit (Proverbs 8:29); so the boundary moves far out, or the decree is taken far away. The Greek has that day will rub away your statutes. Matsor, Egypt, is the name in the streams of Egypt (Isaiah 19:6), and it is also the word siege (5:1): those who once laid siege send the people home. The Greek has from Tyre. From sea to sea… the River is the reach of the king's rule in May he rule from sea to sea, and from the River to the ends of the earth (Psalm 72:8). Ha-arets is the land and the earth; here it follows the lands of v12, and is given as the earth. The fruit of their deeds is Jeremiah's phrase (Jeremiah 17:10).

  • vv18–19 "Who is a God like You, carrying guilt and passing over transgression… into the depths of the sea" — mi el kamokha is the song at the sea, Who is like You among the gods, LORD? (Exodus 15:11), and the question in the prophet's own name: Mikhah is written Mikhayah in Jeremiah 26:18, who is like YH?, and Micaiah son of Imlah (1 Kings 22:8) bears the same name. Nose avon, carrying guilt, is the name the LORD proclaimed, carrying guilt and rebellion and sin (Exodus 34:7). Over al pesha, passing over transgression, is the phrase of it is his glory to overlook an offense (Proverbs 19:11); Amos heard I will never again pass them by (Amos 7:8), and here the LORD passes over the sin instead. La-ad, forever, has the letters of le-ed, for a witness, and the Greek has He did not keep His anger as a witness. Yikhbosh, He will tread under foot, is the verb of fill the earth and take it under foot (Genesis 1:28). Metsulot, depths, is the sea where Pharaoh's army sank, They went down into the depths like a stone (Exodus 15:5). The Hebrew has their sins where the Greek has our sins.
